subject: Optimize Toolkit: packaging, pilot credits, and quantization guidance
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Optimize Toolkit: packaging, pilot credits, and quantization guidance

Hi Susan —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. ClearBay's use case (customer-facing summarization + retrieval for support articles) maps nicely to a low-latency, cost-sensitive pilot. A few things I wanted to put on the table so we can align on a fast pilot:

- Proposed pilot scope: 3 months, up to 50k generated tokens/day average (burst up to 200k/day), embeddings for retrieval at ~10k requests/day.
- Technical knobs we recommend: enable prefix/KV cache for repeated conversational contexts; use int8 quantization for gen model (saves ~45% cost on our infra with <2% delta on our eval set); use fp16 for embeddings.
- Commercials we suggest for the pilot: 40% usage credit applied to host API for the pilot period, flat support package, and a follow-on committed discount if you convert to a Dedicated pool (tiered by commit band).

Attached is a short term-sheet stub (optimize-pilot-term-sheet.pdf) and a one-page quantization note (quant-recs-brief.pdf). Can you confirm the expected pilot volume and whether we should include SOC2 evidence up front? If you want pricing broken down to days and per-endpoint TCO, we can get that to you tomorrow.

Next steps: if that sounds reasonable, I'll loop in our finance lead and draft a mutual action plan with milestones + success criteria.

Best,
Rafael

Rafael — thanks, this looks promising. A couple quick questions from our side: 

1) How does int8 affect the hallucination rate for longer summaries (700-1,000 tokens)? We care about quality more than token savings for escalations.
2) For KV caching: does that apply to session-level state only, or can we safely cache across users for identical prompts?
3) SOC2 evidence: yes, we need that before legal signs anything. Can you include the SOC2 artifact and a short note on data retention controls?

Volume: initial pilot expected to land around 30k gen tokens/day and 5k embeddings/day, but we may step up after month 1 depending on latency.

If you can send a clarified TCO and a sample MAP we can review with procurement early next week.

—Susan

Susan — quick answers inline, and Kim/Marcus feel free to jump in.

> 1) How does int8 affect the hallucination rate for longer summaries (700-1,000 tokens)?
Short answer: our internal evals on similar summarization prompts show median quality delta of ~1.2% BLEU-like score drop and very small increase in factuality errors on long tails. For the first 90 days of a pilot we recommend: enable int8 for generation but keep a small sample of critical flows on fp16 (we can route those by intent). That lets you get the cost benefit while protecting high-stakes responses.

> 2) For KV caching: does that apply to session-level state only, or can we safely cache across users for identical prompts?
KV/prefix caching in our runtime supports both. By default we scope caches to session/user to avoid leakage. We can create a shared-cache layer for identical, public prompts (e.g., canned FAQs) — that requires explicit config in the MAP and a short privacy review.

> 3) SOC2 evidence: yes, we need that before legal signs anything.
We can provide the SOC2 package (redwood-soc2-2025.zip) and a one-page data retention control summary. Attaching soc2-evidence.zip here — contains an index and the auditor letter.

Commercial proposal (pilot):
- Pilot credits: Redwood provides credits equal to 40% of expected pilot bill (estimate based on your 30k gen / 5k embed/day usage). Credits apply to hosted API usage only and expire at pilot end.
- Conversion path: if you convert to Dedicated within 90 days post-pilot we offer a credit back of unused pilot credits applied to first month of Dedicated committed invoice up to $15k.
- Post-pilot committed discount bands (illustrative): 10% off list at 6–12k committed tokens/day, 18% off at 12–25k, 25% at >25k (subject to term lengths).

Operational guardrails:
- We will include a canary routing policy so critical intents can be forced to fp16 for the first 2 weeks.
- Implementation play: 2-week integration (SDK + routing), 1 week bake, then ramp.

Attachments: updated quant notes (quant-recs-brief.pdf) and the SOC2 bundle (soc2-evidence.zip).

Next steps: I will draft the MAP and a short TCO table (per-endpoint cost at current estimate) and share a Google Doc link — target EOD today. If procurement wants a payment schedule, Kim can draft a one-page term addendum.

Best,
Rafael

Attachment: quant-recs-brief.pdf (PDF, 1 page)
Attachment: soc2-evidence.zip (ZIP, index + auditor letter)
